problem_statement: This repo (rebranded here as the one-page marketing site for Tidewheel Ferry Company, a passenger and bicycle ferry that crosses Marrow Reach between Cathster Quay and the Weir Head landing) is a static, self-contained site served directly from site/index.html plus local static/css, static/js and static/images (no build step). The site now spans the scroll-anchored home page (index.html) and two secondary pages, timetable.html and fares.html, that share the same top navigation and chrome. A 'From the crossing log' section was added to the home page beneath the masthead, hosting a four-tile metric strip (crossings run this season, years working the reach, berths at the two landings, bicycles carried on a busy day), a sailing-window filter (All sailings / Early run / Midday run / Late run) with a '#sailing-readout', and a shared 'Reaches we work' rail. Deliver a coordinated repair while keeping the navy/rust theme, section order, copy and DOM intact: (1) REPAIR the metric strip's responsive layout so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow — the strip's row is currently pinned to a fixed 720px non-wrapping width with fixed 170px tiles, dragging the whole document sideways; do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden, the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. (2) Promote the 'Reaches we work' rail (Cathster Quay / Weir Head landing / Saltmarsh reach chips) into a shared component that appears CONSISTENTLY on the home crossing-log section AND on the timetable.html AND fares.html pages, styled to match the Tidewheel ivory/navy palette (light ivory surface, restrained border, rust-on-ivory chips) — the rendered rail must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette dark slab. (3) Wire the sailing-window filter end to end: clicking a window button (Early run / Midday run / Late run) must update the '#sailing-readout' to 'Showing: <selected window>' in addition to highlighting the active button — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected window, not the default 'Showing: All sailings'. Keep the navigation header, masthead, About, Crossings, How-a-crossing-works, Routes, Testimonials, Crew, Contact and footer sections present and unchanged, keep the secondary pages reachable (real routes, not 404), and keep the site static with a clean browser console (no remote font/CDN/map requests) and the desktop/tablet layouts intact.
required_content: The 'From the crossing log' metric strip renders its four tiles (crossings run this season, years working the reach, berths at the two landings, bicycles carried on a busy day) within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px, and remains intact on desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px).

A shared 'Reaches we work' rail (Cathster Quay / Weir Head landing / Saltmarsh reach chips) appears CONSISTENTLY on the home crossing-log section AND on the timetable.html AND fares.html pages — the same rail component in all three places, not only on the home page.

The 'Reaches we work' rail keeps the Tidewheel ivory/navy palette (light ivory surface, restrained border, rust-on-ivory chips) and is visually faithful to the reference rendering on the home and secondary pages — not a collapsed or off-palette dark slab.

The sailing-window filter is wired end to end: clicking a window button updates the '#sailing-readout' to 'Showing: <selected window>' (e.g. clicking Early run sets 'Showing: Early run') in addition to marking the button active; the post-click terminal state reflects the selected window, not the default 'Showing: All sailings'.
The timetable.html and fares.html secondary pages share the home navigation and remain reachable (real routes, not 404).

The navigation header, masthead, About, Crossings, How-a-crossing-works, Routes, Testimonials, Crew, Contact and footer remain present and unchanged in content and structure, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote font/CDN/map errors).
design_constraints: Fix the responsive layout of the crossing-log metric strip; do not delete the strip, change its four tiles, or restyle unrelated sections. The repair must not depend on hiding overflow at the body/html level or clipping content off-screen.

Add the SAME shared 'Reaches we work' rail component to the home crossing-log section, the timetable.html page AND the fares.html page so the reach language is consistent site-wide; do not add it to only one page.
Preserve the template's design language: the navy/rust accent, the condensed section headings, the full-bleed masthead, the section rhythm and order; the rail must render in the ivory/navy palette.
Keep the sailing-window filter interaction wired end to end (the #sailing-readout terminal readout must reflect the clicked window), not merely a class toggle.

Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console, and the secondary pages must share the same nav and stay real routes.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the one-page site at 1440px: the navigation header, masthead, and the 'From the crossing log' band all fit with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_home captures the same page at 390px: with the defect the metrics band forces the document ~338px wider than the viewport; the repair brings horizontal overflow within tolerance.
tablet_home captures the page at 834px, where the band already fits and must continue to fit after the repair.
mobile_services captures the 390px page scrolled to the Crossings section, verifying the whole document (including the band above it) no longer overflows horizontally.
desktop_services, desktop_projects, desktop_team, and desktop_contacts confirm the section content and structure are unchanged by the repair.

change_completion: The crossing-log metric strip renders its four tiles within the viewport on mobile.
The shared 'Reaches we work' rail appears on the home crossing-log section, the timetable.html page AND the fares.html page.
The sailing-window filter click updates the #sailing-readout terminal readout to the selected window.
design_consistency: The navy/rust palette, section rhythm, order, and navigation are preserved.
The 'Reaches we work' rail keeps the ivory/navy look and is visually faithful to the reference across the home and secondary pages.
responsive: At 390px the crossing-log metric strip wraps or shrinks so the document stays within the viewport (no horizontal overflow beyond 24px), including the mobile timetable page.
At 834px and 1440px the strip lays out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
regression: Navigation, masthead, About, Crossings, How-a-crossing-works, Routes, Testimonials, Crew, Contact and footer remain present and unchanged; the sailing-window filter readout reflects the clicked window rather than the default.
The static site serves from index.html + timetable.html + fares.html with a clean console and no remote requests.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static one-page marketing task (website-templates marketing-agency template rebranded as Tidewheel Ferry Company) hardened to true-new-L4 by manufacturing two real secondary pages (timetable.html + fares.html) that share the site navigation. The reference (a) repairs the crossing-log metric strip so it WRAPS fluidly on mobile (flex 1 1 140px -> 0 overflow), (b) promotes a shared 'Reaches we work' rail into the home crossing-log section AND the timetable.html AND fares.html pages in the Tidewheel ivory/navy palette, and (c) wires the sailing-window filter so #sailing-readout reflects the clicked window. The baseline is the original layout defect: a fixed 720px nowrap strip (overflows mobile ~338px), NO rail anywhere (D2 fails on all three pages, D3 fails) but the sailing-filter JS is CORRECT (baseline PASSES D4 -> leg-orthogonal). The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the strip to a 540px min-width row + overflow-x:hidden on the row (still overflows the document ~150px -> D6 fail, gotcha#29 no margin:auto self-clamp), adds the rail to the HOME page only (D2 cross-page fail on timetable + fares), restyles the rail into a collapsed dark-slate slab (D3 visual_regression fail: rail block color_delta_e large, plus rail absent entirely on the timetable page), and toggles the filter's .active class without re-syncing #sailing-readout (click succeeds but the readout stays 'Showing: All sailings' -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). bad fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. Only static/css/crossinglog.css, static/js/sailing-filter.js and the per-page rail presence differ across legs; the site chrome, copy and DOM are otherwise byte-identical. The remote Google Fonts link and the orlovmax.com footer credit are removed as declared INFRA (identical across the three legs) so captures show 0 console and 0 network errors.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: A runnable, self-contained static one-page marketing template (prebuilt HTML/CSS/JS served directly from build/) rebranded to Tidewheel Ferry Company; a newly added metrics band introduces a mobile horizontal-overflow regression, making it an ideal host for a repair/state_continuity task whose sole discriminator is no_horizontal_overflow with content and DOM held identical across legs.
